title: Converged observability TF module for VPC: Prometheus + Grafana, OTEL collector, and fault-tolerant log-shipping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Current VPC observability provisioning is fragmented across several Terraform modules and Helm releases with inconsistent healthchecks, limited upgrade safety, and brittle log-forwarding failure modes. Goal: create a single converged Terraform module that provisions an opinionated observability pipeline inside customer VPCs: Prometheus (federation-friendly), Grafana (managed dashboards + provisioning), an OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel) as a resilient ingestion layer, and a log-shipping subsystem with built-in retries/backpressure handling. The module should be lifecycle-safe (rolling upgrades, canary hooks), provide health-check endpoints and reconciliation hints, and expose minimal, well-documented variables for customers. It must support both Kubernetes (Helm or Kustomize) and ECS/Fargate variants via providers and produce clear outputs for onboarding Redwood Console to consume.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Terraform module named redwood_vpc_observability exists and can be initialized and applied against a sandbox VPC without manual steps.
2) Prometheus deployed with serviceMonitor-friendly scrape discovery and federation endpoints documented.
3) Grafana provisioned with two baseline dashboards and an admin user secret output.
4) OTEL collector deployed with a HA deployment (multi-replica + readiness/liveness probes) and a configurable receivers/processors/exporters chain.
5) Log-shipping subsystem supports at-least-once delivery with exponential backoff and dead-lettering to S3.
6) Upgrade plan supports in-place rolling upgrades with automated canaries and metrics-based rollback triggers.
7) Module exposes healthcheck endpoints and a terraform null_resource reconcile hook to validate runtime component health post-upgrade.
8) Automated terratest suite validates module apply/destroy and a smoke test that sends synthetic telemetry and verifies it appears in Prometheus/Grafana/Log storage.
9) Documentation and example usage in examples/ directory for Kubernetes and ECS variants.
10) Security review completed and KMS integration documented.
design_decisions:
- Use Helm provider with pinned chart versions for Prometheus/Grafana to reduce drift; override only necessary values via values.yaml templating.
- Deploy OTEL Collector as a Deployment with an init container that verifies schema compatibility for exporters; allow switch to daemonset for high-cardinality node metrics.
- Log shipping implemented as a dedicated Fluent Bit/Logagent Helm chart with output to a buffer queue backed by persistent volume or S3 buffering depending on environment.
- Provide a small Kubernetes operator-style reconcile hook (implemented as a terraform null_resource + local-exec script) that validates health endpoints and emits formatted logs to the apply output.
- Canary rollout implemented by templating deployment replica counts and using a metric-checker job that validates error_rate < threshold for N minutes before scaling remainder.
- Keep module inputs minimal: region, vpc_id, namespace, log_retention_days, prometheus_retention, grafana_admin_email, kms_key_id, enable_s3_dlq. All other tuning via optional map var.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (sandbox): implement module and examples, run terratest. Phase 2 (staging): onboard one internal staging VPC and run rolling upgrade from existing helm releases to the module-managed resources with canary disabled. Phase 3 (production pilot): enable canary rollouts for low-risk production cell and run traffic injection tests. Phase 4 (broad rollout): document migration steps for customers and add automated migration script (helm->tf) to module tools. Rollback: terraform plan will include computed changes and the canary metric-checker will trigger scale-down/restore if thresholds breached. Preserve old helm releases during canary until final cutover.
test_plan:
- Unit: terraform validate and fmt checks in CI.
- Integration: terratest applies against a dedicated sandbox account that runs full apply->smoke->destroy.
- Canary test harness: simulate telemetry (metrics + traces + logs) using a lightweight load generator; verify latency and ingestion counts.
- Chaos: kill one OTEL collector replica and confirm readiness probe triggers replacement and no data loss beyond a short window.
- Upgrade: run chart and collector upgrades in test cluster using pipeline jobs that validate outputs and run metric-based acceptance tests.
- Security: run static scan for secrets, validate KMS integration, ensure IAM least-privilege policy provided in module.
- Nightly: drift detection job that runs terraform plan and alerts if drift detected for customer-managed modules.
notes: PM flagged timeline dependency on Private Deployments Q4 launch; coordinate with product for release gating.
Prefer smaller, well-documented variable surface area to avoid customer misconfiguration.
Consider adding an optional grafana sidecar for provisioning additional dashboards via github sync in a follow-up ticket.
We should reuse existing sentinel/obs-module healthhooks where possible but keep new module independent to avoid coupling.
Estimate conservative due to canary automation and testing matrix across k8s/ECS variants.
